brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.requirement: Shelf unit for books (multi-level shelving / storage surface)
requirements.evidence: Built 3-storey hex structure (15 bases: pieces at 0,0 / 0,1 / 1,0 plus half-n fronts at 0,-1 / 1,-1 across levels 0-2, with snaps). Top level capped with 5 covers (cover:0,-1,2;half-n, cover:0,0,2;full, cover:0,1,2;full, cover:1,-1,2;half-n, cover:1,0,2;full) forming continuous deck f22 (~310×310 mm) plus lower storeys for shelving. Caps applied to open faces and joints locked. Book-stack prop (prop:1) placed on deck visible in both look views.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: Configurator verifies only fit/collisions (check_build ok, meshClash clear). Load rating, strength, material, print settings and assembly quality are outside its scope. Parts are 3D-printed plastic chosen by user — no 50 kg rating can be guaranteed or verified here. Shape provides shelf surfaces (partial help) but must not be relied on for heavy loads without independent engineering and testing.
Two drawers installed at ground level: drawer:0#0,-1#cut (at 0,-1,0) and drawer:0#1,-1#cut (at 1,-1,0) on half-n bases, with compartment floors (f7/f15) available for small items.

finish.summary: Built the form of a 3-level shelf unit with top shelf deck showing books and two front drawers; capped faces and locked joints for a tidy display build. Load rating to 50 kg cannot be met or verified in this 3D-printed modular system - treat as unrated plastic model only and do not load heavily without separate engineering.

M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

result.note: Ask again with a family or a few words (text) to see the parts themselves.

A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base (variant half-n, half-s, half-e or half-w) first. No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
